label: Same Thing, Two Descriptions. The boot is described first by pixel intensities, then by task-useful features.
Encoder and Head. The encoder builds a representation and the head uses it.
A Hierarchy of Features. A conceptual hierarchy from local edges to larger combinations.
Three Routes to a Representation. The reference run compares representations with the same kind of linear probe and 10,000 probe labels.
A CNN at a Glance. The exact lesson architecture: 1×28×28 → 16×28×28 → 16×14×14 → 32×14×14 → 32×7×7 → 1,568 features → a classifier.
Follow a grid into a vector: a numerical worked example.
Slide one shared filter: a numerical worked example.
Growing Receptive Fields. For this model, receptive-field widths grow from 3 after conv1 to 4 after pool1, 8 after conv2, and 10 after pool2.
What Each Part of a CNN Contributes. Convolution applies local shared weights; feature maps retain spatial organisation, pooling reduces resolution, and the head combines features into class scores.
From Text to Embeddings. Token IDs are arbitrary vocabulary indices.
An Embedding Is a Lookup Table. Selecting row 49 is equivalent to multiplying a one-hot vector by the table, without materialising that dense one-hot vector.
Cosine Similarity Is About Angle. Cosine similarity compares directions rather than lengths: 1 for the same direction, 0 for perpendicular vectors, and −1 for opposite directions.
Static vs. Contextual. A static table returns the same vector for a token type in every sentence.
One Table, Two Objectives. Illustrative geometry, not the experiment’s measured projection.
